<a id="commandhistory"></a>

## `CommandHistory`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.CommandHistory` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The lines already typed, and the Up/Down cursor over them. A ring: once [`CommandHistory.Capacity`](#commandhistory--capacity) lines are held, the oldest is dropped.

The draft matters as much as the history: pressing Up must not lose the half-typed line, so the first Up remembers it and coming back down past the newest entry restores it.

Lines kept when no capacity is given.

How many lines it currently holds.

<a id="commandhistory--entries"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Entries { get; }`

The lines it holds, oldest first. Never null.

<a id="commandhistory--add"></a>

### `bool Add(string line)`

Records a submitted line and puts the cursor back on the live line. A blank line is ignored, and so is a line identical to the most recent one - holding Enter on the same command should not push everything else out of the ring.

**Parameters**

- `line`: The line that was submitted.

**Returns:** True when the line was added.

<a id="commandhistory--clear"></a>

Forgets every line.

<a id="commandhistory--next"></a>

### `string Next()`

Down: the entry after the one shown now, or the remembered draft once the cursor comes back past the newest entry. Returns null when the cursor is already on the live line.

<a id="commandhistory--previous"></a>

Up: the entry before the one shown now. The first call remembers `currentLine` as the draft. Returns null when there is nothing older, which the caller should read as "leave the input alone".

**Parameters**

- `currentLine`: What is in the input box right now.

<a id="commandhistory--resetcursor"></a>

Puts the cursor back on the live line and forgets the draft.

<a id="commandlineparser"></a>

## `CommandLineParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.CommandLineParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Splits a console line into tokens. Whitespace separates, `"` and `'` quote a token that contains spaces, and `\` escapes the next character (so a literal quote or backslash can be typed). Single quotes are literal inside: `'C:\path'` is one token spelled exactly like that, which is what a person typing a path expects.

Unity-free and deterministic, so the awkward cases - an empty quoted argument, an unterminated quote, a trailing backslash - are covered by unit tests rather than found in-game.

<a id="commandlineparser--danglingescapeerror"></a>

### `const string DanglingEscapeError = "the line ends with a lone backslash"`

What [`CommandLineParser.TryTokenize`](#commandlineparser--trytokenize) reports for a line ending in a lone backslash.

<a id="commandlineparser--unterminatedquoteerror"></a>

### `const string UnterminatedQuoteError = "unterminated quote"`

What [`CommandLineParser.TryTokenize`](#commandlineparser--trytokenize) reports for a quote that is never closed.

<a id="commandlineparser--join"></a>

### `static string Join(IReadOnlyList<string> arguments, int startIndex = 0)`

Joins arguments back into one string with single spaces - what a command that takes free text (`log`, `subtitle`) wants from the tokens it was handed.

**Parameters**

- `arguments`: The arguments; null yields an empty string.
- `startIndex`: First argument to include; out-of-range yields an empty string.

<a id="commandlineparser--parse"></a>

### `static ParsedCommand Parse(string line)`

Splits a line into a command and its arguments, or null when the line holds no command at all (blank, or nothing but whitespace).

**Parameters**

- `line`: The line as typed.

<a id="commandlineparser--tokenize"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> Tokenize(string line)`

Splits a line, tolerating the mistakes a person makes while typing: an unterminated quote simply runs to the end of the line and a trailing backslash is dropped. Never throws. Use [`CommandLineParser.TryTokenize`](#commandlineparser--trytokenize) when the mistake should be reported instead.

**Parameters**

- `line`: The line as typed; null or blank yields no tokens.

<a id="commandlineparser--trytokenize"></a>

### `static bool TryTokenize(string line, out IReadOnlyList<string> tokens, out string error)`

Splits a line and reports the first problem found. The tokens are produced either way (the tolerant reading), so a caller can show both the result and the warning.

**Parameters**

- `line`: The line as typed.
- `tokens`: The tokens; never null, possibly empty.
- `error`: Null when the line was well-formed, otherwise what was wrong.

**Returns:** True when the line was well-formed.

<a id="commandregistry"></a>

## `CommandRegistry`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.CommandRegistry` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The commands the in-game console knows. A registry is an ordinary object so it can be unit-tested in isolation; [`CommandRegistry.Shared`](#commandregistry--shared) is the one the running game uses, because the plugins that contribute commands are separate BepInEx assemblies with no reference to one another (the same reason `SmokeRegistry` is process-wide).

Every member takes the same lock, so a mod registering a command from its Awake while the console renders on the main thread is safe.

## `Completion`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.Completion` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Tab completion: prefix first, and only when nothing starts with what was typed, a fuzzy pass that accepts the letters in order with gaps (`pl` finds `packs list`'s `packs`, `mdt` finds `masterdata`). Unity-free, so every rule here is a unit test rather than a surprise in-game.

### `static string CommonPrefix(IReadOnlyList<string> matches, string typed = null)`

The longest prefix every match shares, never shorter than what was already typed.

- `typed`: What was typed; returned when the matches share nothing more.

<a id="completion--complete"></a>

### `static CompletionResult Complete(string typed, IEnumerable<string> candidates)`

Completes what has been typed against a set of candidates.

**Parameters**

- `typed`: The word being completed. Null or empty offers every candidate, sorted, and completes to their common prefix.
- `candidates`: The possible words; null entries and duplicates are ignored.

<a id="completion--isfuzzymatch"></a>

- `candidate`: The candidate word.

<a id="consolecolorrole"></a>

## `ConsoleColorRole`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleColorRole` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The colour family a console line belongs to. The families are the ones the terminal viewer uses (`tools/mac/watch-log.py`, table `TAGS`), so a line reads the same in the game and in the terminal; only the colours differ, because in the game they come from the game's own UI palette.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="consolecolorrole--output"></a>`Output` | 0 | A command's own result text. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--echo"></a>`Echo` | 1 | The line the user typed, echoed back. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--satone"></a>`Satone` | 2 | Satone: SPEECH, SAY, STATE, SUBTITLE, FACE, MOTION, LOOK, RESTORE. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--world"></a>`World` | 3 | The game world: MUSIC, POMODORO, SCENARIO, SCENE, WINDOW, LANGUAGE. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--player"></a>`Player` | 4 | The player and good news: READY, BUTTON, TYPED, CLICK, a passing SMOKE. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--content"></a>`Content` | 5 | Content the framework moved: DATA, VOICE, TEXTURE, MASTERDATA. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--framework"></a>`Framework` | 6 | The framework talking about itself: CONSOLE, SETUP, TRACE, KEYS, PACKS, NOTE and anything unknown. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--warning"></a>`Warning` | 7 | Worth a look: HEALTH, WARN, a Warning line. |
| <a id="consolecolorrole--error"></a>`Error` | 8 | Something failed: UNITY, ERROR, a bad HEALTH reading, a failed SMOKE, an Error line. |

## `ConsoleCommand`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleCommand` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

One command the in-game console can run: how it is typed, what it does, and the work itself. Pure data plus a delegate, so the whole command layer is unit-testable without Unity - the handler is supplied by whoever registers the command.

<a id="consolecommand--ctor"></a>

### `ConsoleCommand(string name, string description, string usage, string group, Func<IReadOnlyList<string>, string> handler)`

Creates a command.

**Parameters**

- `name`: What the user types, e.g. `packs`. Required, matched case-insensitively, and must contain no whitespace (the first token of the line is the name).
- `description`: One short sentence shown by `help`. Null becomes empty.
- `usage`: The argument shape, e.g. `packs list|rescan`. Null or empty becomes `name`, so `help` always has something to print.
- `group`: Heading `help` lists the command under, e.g. `framework`. Null or blank becomes [`ConsoleCommand.DefaultGroup`](#consolecommand--defaultgroup).
- `handler`: The work. Receives the arguments after the name (never null, possibly empty) and returns what to print (null or empty prints nothing). It may throw: the registry turns an exception into an error line rather than letting it reach the game's frame.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `name` is null, blank or contains whitespace.
- `ArgumentNullException`: `handler` is null.

<a id="consoleescapeguard"></a>

## `ConsoleEscapeGuard`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleEscapeGuard` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Keeps the game from acting on an Escape the CWY console already used. The game reads Escape itself every frame and switches a fullscreen window to windowed mode (`RoomGameManager.Update` → `SettingService.ChangeWindowMode(Window)`); with the console open, the same press must only close the console.

Unity does not order two components' `Update` calls, so the game may read Escape before or after the console handles it in the same frame. Both orders are covered:

- The console ran first: it called [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Claim`](#consoleescapeguard--claim) for this frame before closing.
- The game ran first: the console is still open, and its latest word on who owns Escape ([`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Observe`](#consoleescapeguard--observe), made every frame it is on screen) says the console, and that word is from this frame or the one before.

Only a switch *to windowed* in a frame where Escape went down is ever blocked, so the settings window's own Window button (a click) is never affected. Main thread only; the state is two frame numbers.

<a id="consoleescapeguard--noframe"></a>

### `const int NoFrame = -2147483648`

Frame number meaning "never".

<a id="consoleescapeguard--blockedcount"></a>

### `long BlockedCount { get; }`

How many window switches [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.ShouldBlockWindowedSwitch`](#consoleescapeguard--shouldblockwindowedswitch) has blocked.

<a id="consoleescapeguard--claimedframe"></a>

### `int ClaimedFrame { get; }`

The frame of the latest [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Claim`](#consoleescapeguard--claim), or [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.NoFrame`](#consoleescapeguard--noframe).

<a id="consoleescapeguard--observedframe"></a>

### `int ObservedFrame { get; }`

The frame of the latest [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Observe`](#consoleescapeguard--observe), or [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.NoFrame`](#consoleescapeguard--noframe).

<a id="consoleescapeguard--observedowner"></a>

### `EscapeOwner ObservedOwner { get; }`

The owner the latest [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.Observe`](#consoleescapeguard--observe) reported.

<a id="consoleescapeguard--claim"></a>

### `void Claim(int frame)`

Records that the console used this frame's Escape (it is about to close).

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame number.

<a id="consoleescapeguard--observe"></a>

### `void Observe(int frame, EscapeOwner owner)`

Records who owns Escape this frame. Call once a frame while the console is on screen.

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame number.
- `owner`: The owner ([`ConsoleEscapeGuard.OwnerOf`](#consoleescapeguard--ownerof)).

<a id="consoleescapeguard--ownerof"></a>

### `static EscapeOwner OwnerOf(bool consoleOpen, bool interactable, ConsoleFocus focus)`

Who owns Escape right now, by the console's own key routing ([`ConsoleKeyRouter.Route`](#consolekeyrouter--route)): the console when it is on screen, interactable, and Escape would close it; also the console while its own input is composing (Escape then cancels the composition inside the console). The game otherwise - including while the player types into one of the game's own text fields.

**Parameters**

- `consoleOpen`: The console is open.
- `interactable`: The console takes input (not faded out with the game's hidden UI).
- `focus`: Who has the keyboard.

<a id="consoleescapeguard--reset"></a>

### `void Reset()`

Forgets every observation and claim. For tests and a console rebuild.

<a id="consoleescapeguard--shouldblockwindowedswitch"></a>

### `bool ShouldBlockWindowedSwitch(int frame, bool toWindowed, bool escapeDown, bool consoleOpen)`

True when the game's switch to windowed mode must be skipped because the console used this frame's Escape. Counts every block in [`ConsoleEscapeGuard.BlockedCount`](#consoleescapeguard--blockedcount).

**Parameters**

- `frame`: Unity's frame number.
- `toWindowed`: The game asked for windowed mode.
- `escapeDown`: Escape went down this frame.
- `consoleOpen`: The console is open right now.

<a id="consolekeyrouter"></a>

## `ConsoleKeyRouter`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleKeyRouter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Decides who owns a key while the console is on screen: the console, the text field, the input method, the hotkey registry or the game. Pure, so every rule is unit-tested.

The console's input is a real UI text field, so while it is selected the framework's hotkey registry stands down on its own - it ignores every chord while any text field has focus (`Hotkeys.IsTyping`), which is also why a typed letter never reaches the game's own shortcuts. That leaves the console two keys to handle itself: the toggle chord (the registry is not listening while our field is selected) and Escape.

The toggle is claimed only when our field is selected, the exact condition under which the registry is silent, so exactly one of the two acts on a press. The console toggle is also debounced per frame, which covers the frame on which closing deselects the field.

While the input method is composing (Japanese today, Thai later), Escape, Tab, the arrows and the page keys belong to it: they pick candidates and cancel the composition.

<a id="consolekeyrouter--classifytypedchar"></a>

### `static ConsoleTypedChar ClassifyTypedChar(char c, bool control, bool command, bool alt, bool pasting = false)`

What a character the text field is about to insert becomes. Return is a submit; control characters are dropped; so is any character typed with Ctrl (not AltGr, which Windows reports as Ctrl+Alt and which types real characters on many layouts) or with Command held - a chord such as Ctrl+Shift+C must not leave a letter behind. Everything else is kept, including non-ASCII: commands are ASCII today, but a Thai subtitle or an input-method commit must pass through untouched.

**Parameters**

- `c`: The character.
- `control`: A Control key is held.
- `command`: A Command (macOS) key is held.
- `alt`: An Alt / Option key is held.
- `pasting`: The character is part of a paste (Command/Ctrl+V is down; the field appends the clipboard one character at a time with the chord held). Printable characters are kept; line breaks are dropped, so a pasted line is never submitted on its own.

<a id="consolekeyrouter--route"></a>

### `static ConsoleKeyAction Route(ConsoleKeyPress keys, ConsoleFocus focus)`

The single action for this frame's keys, in priority order.

**Parameters**

- `keys`: Keys that went down this frame.
- `focus`: Who has the keyboard.

<a id="consolelayout"></a>

## `ConsoleLayout`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleLayout` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Where the game-style console puts its parts inside the window body: the tab strip along the top, the log area under it, and the bottom row (the command line on the Console tab, the action buttons and the snapshot/live label on the others). Pure, so the rule is tested without an engine and every tab gets the same log area from one place.

Sizes are canvas units at the game's 1920x1080 reference resolution. The text inside the log area keeps [`LineLayout.Padding`](#linelayout--padding) from the area's top and bottom edges.

<a id="consolelinecolors"></a>

## `ConsoleLineColors`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleLineColors` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How a console line is coloured in the game-style console: which family its tag belongs to, which colour that family gets, and the TextMeshPro rich text for the whole line.

The palette is taken from the game's own UI atlas (`UIAtlas`, sampled 2026-09-28): the cyan `#00D5EF` and magenta `#EA00B2` of every hover outline (`t_ui_addbox_active`), the lavender `#9999BF` of the separator bar (`t_ui_back_bar`) and the muted `#6E6E93` of the close icon and of unselected tab labels. The accents are lifted a little where the raw value is too dark to read as 18-point text on the game's 90 % black window.

A mirrored line looks like `TAG primary k=v k=v` (the stamp is dropped by the log mirror). It is drawn the way the terminal viewer draws it: the tag bold in its family colour, the primary column near-white, the fields dim.

<a id="consolelinecolors--fieldtext"></a>

### `static readonly ConsoleRgb FieldText`

The `k=v` column of a tagged line.

<a id="consolelinecolors--gamecyan"></a>

### `static readonly ConsoleRgb GameCyan`

The game's hover-outline cyan.

<a id="consolelinecolors--gamelavender"></a>

### `static readonly ConsoleRgb GameLavender`

The game's separator lavender.

<a id="consolelinecolors--gamemagenta"></a>

### `static readonly ConsoleRgb GameMagenta`

The game's hover-outline magenta.

<a id="consolelinecolors--gamemuted"></a>

### `static readonly ConsoleRgb GameMuted`

The game's muted icon and unselected-tab colour.

<a id="consolelinecolors--primarytext"></a>

### `static readonly ConsoleRgb PrimaryText`

The primary column of a tagged line.

<a id="consolelinecolors--colour"></a>

### `static ConsoleRgb Colour(ConsoleColorRole role)`

The colour of a family.

**Parameters**

- `role`: The family.

<a id="consolelinecolors--escape"></a>

### `static string Escape(string text)`

Wraps text so TextMeshPro draws it literally. A `</noparse>` inside the text is broken with a zero-width space, so it cannot end the literal run early.

**Parameters**

- `text`: Any text; null is empty.

<a id="consolelinecolors--roleof"></a>

### `static ConsoleColorRole RoleOf(ConsoleLineKind kind, string text)`

The family a whole scrollback line belongs to. The line's kind wins where it is decisive (an echo, a command result, a Warning or Error from the log); an Info line is coloured by its tag.

**Parameters**

- `kind`: What the scrollback says the line is.
- `text`: The line's text.

<a id="consolelinecolors--roleoftag"></a>

### `static ConsoleColorRole RoleOfTag(string tag, string primary)`

The family of a tag, with the viewer's two content-dependent rules: a HEALTH line whose primary starts with `spike`, `lowFps` or `lowMemory` and a SMOKE line that starts with `FAIL` or reads `ok=false` are errors.

**Parameters**

- `tag`: A one-word console tag; anything unknown is [`ConsoleColorRole.Framework`](#consolecolorrole--framework).
- `primary`: The primary column, for the two content rules. May be null.

<a id="consolelinecolors--torichtext"></a>

### `static string ToRichText(ConsoleLineKind kind, string text)`

The line as TextMeshPro rich text. Everything that came from the log or a command is inside `<noparse>`, so a `<name>` in a usage line prints as written instead of being read as markup.

**Parameters**

- `kind`: What the scrollback says the line is.
- `text`: The line's text.

<a id="consolelinecolors--trysplit"></a>

### `static bool TrySplit(string text, out string tag, out string primary, out string fields)`

Splits a mirrored line into its columns: `TAG primary fields`. A leading `HH:mm:ss.fff` stamp is skipped, so a raw console-file line splits too.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The line.
- `tag`: The tag, or empty.
- `primary`: The primary column, or empty.
- `fields`: The `k=v` column, or empty when the line has none.

**Returns:** False when the line does not start with a console tag.

<a id="consolepanels"></a>

## `ConsolePanels`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsolePanels` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The extra tabs the in-game console shows. A panel is a name and a function that returns the text to draw; the console calls it once per frame while its tab is open, so it must be cheap and must not block.

Process-wide for the same reason as the command registry: a mod lives in its own BepInEx assembly with no reference to the console's. The game adapter registers "Stream" and "State" this way, which is what keeps game-specific state out of the framework.

<a id="consolepanels--count"></a>

### `static int Count { get; }`

How many panels are registered.

<a id="consolepanels--errorsink"></a>

### `static Action<string> ErrorSink { get; set; }`

Where a panel that throws is reported besides the tab itself. Set by the console feature to the BepInEx log.

<a id="consolepanels--names"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> Names { get; }`

The panel names, in registration order. These become the extra tabs.

<a id="consolepanels--clear"></a>

### `static void Clear()`

Removes every panel. Used by tests; harmless at runtime.

<a id="consolepanels--has"></a>

### `static bool Has(string name)`

True when a panel of this name is registered.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The name to look for.

<a id="consolepanels--register"></a>

### `static void Register(string name, Func<string> render)`

Registers a tab. Registering an existing name replaces its renderer and keeps its position, so a plugin whose Awake runs twice does not produce two identical tabs.

**Parameters**

- `name`: Tab label, e.g. `Stream`. Required; matched case-insensitively.
- `render`: Returns the text to draw. Called on the Unity main thread, once per frame while its tab is open. It may throw - the tab then shows the failure - but it must be quick.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `name` is null or blank.
- `ArgumentNullException`: `render` is null.

<a id="consolepanels--tryrender"></a>

### `static bool TryRender(string name, out string text)`

Renders a panel. Never throws: an unknown name and a renderer that throws both come back as the text to draw, and a failure is also sent to [`ConsolePanels.ErrorSink`](#consolepanels--errorsink) so it survives in the log.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The panel to render.
- `text`: The text to draw; never null.

**Returns:** True when the panel exists and rendered without throwing.

<a id="consolepanels--unregister"></a>

### `static bool Unregister(string name)`

Removes a tab.

**Parameters**

- `name`: The registered name.

**Returns:** True when a panel was removed.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy"></a>

## `ConsoleSurfacePolicy`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleSurfacePolicy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Chooses between the game-style console and the IMGUI fallback, and decides which of those choices are worth a log line. Pure; one instance lives for the session.

The rule: if the game's UI assets cannot be resolved (a game update renamed them, or the room is not loaded yet), fall back to IMGUI and say so *once*; the console must never become unusable. "Once" is per state change, not per attempt: the first fallback is logged, repeated failures are not, a later recovery is logged once, and a fallback after that recovery is logged again. A surface that threw while running is broken for the rest of the session and never tried again.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy--broken"></a>

### `bool Broken { get; }`

True once a game-style surface failed at runtime; it is not tried again this session.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy--brokenreason"></a>

### `string BrokenReason { get; }`

Why the game-style surface is broken, or empty.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy--preferred"></a>

### `ConsoleSurfaceKind Preferred(ConsoleStyle style, bool gameStyleRegistered)`

The surface to try first.

**Parameters**

- `style`: The configured style.
- `gameStyleRegistered`: True when an adapter registered a game-style surface.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy--recordattempt"></a>

### `string RecordAttempt(bool shown, string detail)`

Records one attempt to show the game-style surface. Returns the line to log, or null when this outcome was already reported.

**Parameters**

- `shown`: True when the surface is on screen.
- `detail`: On success, what was built (e.g. which optional assets were missing); on failure, why it could not be shown. Null is allowed.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy--recordconfiguredstyle"></a>

### `string RecordConfiguredStyle(ConsoleStyle style)`

The one line saying the IMGUI console was chosen by configuration, or null when it was already said.

**Parameters**

- `style`: The configured style.

<a id="consolesurfacepolicy--recordfailure"></a>

### `string RecordFailure(string reason)`

Records that the game-style surface threw while running. It is not tried again this session. Returns the line to log, or null when a failure was already recorded.

**Parameters**

- `reason`: What went wrong, e.g. the exception type and message.

<a id="consolevisibility"></a>

## `ConsoleVisibility`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.ConsoleVisibility` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Makes an open console follow the game's "Hide UI" button, without ever becoming unreachable. Pure; one instance lives for the session.

The game hides its whole UI by fading the `UI` object's CanvasGroup to 0 and deactivating it (`UIShowManagerForPC.DeactivateUIParent`), and brings it back on the next click (`RoomGameManager`, state Idle). An open console fades with it, so a clean screenshot stays clean.

The user's toggle always wins: pressing it while the console is faded out reveals it instead of closing an invisible window, and opening the console while the UI is hidden shows it straight away. The reveal lasts until the game's UI comes back.

<a id="consolevisibility--hiddenthreshold"></a>

**Parameters**

**Parameters**

- `gameUiAlpha`: How visible the game's UI is, 0 to 1.

<a id="gamestyleassetset"></a>

## `GameStyleAssetSet`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.GameStyleAssetSet` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The game UI assets a game-style window is built from, by name, and the rule for which of them it cannot do without. Names as observed in game 1.17.2: the game's sprite assets and the `UI_FacilityNote` window in the game's RoomScene.

Assets are looked up by name rather than through the game's own windows, so nothing of the game's UI logic (DOTween, VContainer injection, localisation behaviours) comes along, and a game update that renames one sprite degrades one part instead of breaking the window.

<a id="linelayout"></a>

## `LineLayout`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.LineLayout` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which lines a scrolling line view draws, and where, when lines have different heights (a wrapped line is several rows tall; a row in a fallback font can be taller). Pure, so the rules can be tested without an engine; `GameStyleTextView` measures the lines and applies the plan.

The plan pins one edge exactly and lets the other edge clip. Scrolled to the top (and whenever every line fits), line 0 starts at the box's top edge and the text grows down; anywhere else - following the newest line, or scrolled part-way - the chosen bottom line ends at the box's bottom edge and the text grows up. The pinned edge never clips and never leaves a gap; the other edge may show part of a line, which the view's mask cuts at the box edge. Pinning by alignment (rather than by adding up heights) is what keeps the pinned line exact even when a measurement is a little off.

Heights follow TextMeshPro's own stacking (TMP\_Text.CalculatePreferredValues in the game's Unity.TextMeshPro): a line measured on its own spans its first row's ascender to its last row's descender, and consecutive lines are `spacing` apart (the font's line gap), so a run of n lines is the sum of their heights plus (n - 1) spacings.

<a id="linelayout--fittolerance"></a>

### `const float FitTolerance = 0.5f`

How far a line may overshoot the box and still count as wholly visible (measurement rounding).

<a id="linelayout--padding"></a>

### `const float Padding = 8.0f`

Gap between a text box and the panel around it, top and bottom, in canvas units: the game's note window (`UI_FacilityNote` in the game's RoomScene, v1.17.2) keeps its body text 7.3 units above and 8.2 units inside its outlined background (text area insets plus TMP margins), with the mask on the same edge. Rounded to 8.

<a id="linelayout--plan"></a>

### `static LineWindow Plan(int total, int offset, float boxHeight, float spacing, Func<int, float> heightOf)`

Plans the lines to draw.

**Parameters**

- `total`: Lines in the list.
- `offset`: Wanted scroll position in lines above the newest line: 0 follows the newest line; any value at or above the maximum (e.g. `Int32.MaxValue`) means "line 0 at the top". Clamped.
- `boxHeight`: Height of the text box (inside the padding).
- `spacing`: Distance between one line's last row and the next line's first row.
- `heightOf`: Height of line i on its own at the box's width; NaN or negative counts as 0.

<a id="linelayout--runheight"></a>

### `static float RunHeight(int start, int end, float spacing, Func<int, float> heightOf)`

Height of lines \[start, end) stacked: their heights plus a spacing between each pair.

**Parameters**

- `start`: First line.
- `end`: One past the last line.
- `spacing`: Distance between consecutive lines.
- `heightOf`: Height of line i on its own.

<a id="linescroll"></a>

## `LineScroll`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.LineScroll` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Scrolling by whole lines through a list that only grows at the end - the console's scrollback, a panel's text. Pure, so the rules can be tested without an engine.

The position is an *offset from the newest line*: 0 means "showing the newest lines and following them", N means "N lines above that". Counting from the bottom is what makes following the tail free - a new line at offset 0 simply appears - and what lets a view the user scrolled up stay on the same lines while more arrive ([`LineScrollState`](#linescrollstate)).

`Range`, `Follow` and `Capacity` were removed: the text view measures every line ([`LineLayout`](#linelayout)), so only tests called them.

Only the visible lines are ever handed to the text renderer. A single TextMeshPro mesh holds at most 65,535 vertices (about 16,000 characters), which a full 300-line scrollback can exceed, so rendering the whole buffer and letting a ScrollRect move it is not an option.

<a id="linescroll--minhandlesize"></a>

### `const float MinHandleSize = 0.05f`

Smallest scrollbar handle, as a share of the track, so it stays grabbable.

<a id="linescroll--clamp"></a>

**Parameters**

- `offset`: The wanted offset.
- `total`: Lines in the list.
- `visible`: Lines the view shows at once.

<a id="linescroll--handlesize"></a>

### `static float HandleSize(int total, int visible)`

The scrollbar handle's size as a share of the track: what fraction of the list is visible, never below [`LineScroll.MinHandleSize`](#linescroll--minhandlesize).

**Parameters**

- `total`: Lines in the list.
- `visible`: Lines the view shows at once.

<a id="linescroll--maxoffset"></a>

### `static int MaxOffset(int total, int visible)`

The largest offset: the oldest line at the top of the view.

**Parameters**

- `total`: Lines in the list.
- `visible`: Lines the view shows at once.

<a id="linescroll--offsetfromscrollbar"></a>

### `static int OffsetFromScrollbar(float value, int total, int visible)`

The offset a scrollbar value stands for; the inverse of [`LineScroll.ScrollbarValue`](#linescroll--scrollbarvalue).

**Parameters**

- `value`: Scrollbar value, 0 (newest) to 1 (oldest). Out-of-range values are clamped.
- `total`: Lines in the list.
- `visible`: Lines the view shows at once.

<a id="linescroll--page"></a>

### `static int Page(int visible)`

How far one PageUp or PageDown moves: a screen, less one line of context.

**Parameters**

<a id="linescroll--scrollbarvalue"></a>

### `static float ScrollbarValue(int offset, int total, int visible)`

The scrollbar value for an offset, for a bottom-to-top scrollbar: 0 is the newest line (handle at the bottom), 1 the oldest (handle at the top).

**Parameters**

- `offset`: Offset from the newest line.
- `total`: Lines in the list.

<a id="linescrollstate"></a>

## `LineScrollState`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.LineScrollState` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Where a line view is scrolled to, and what the reader asked for: follow the newest line, stay on the lines being read, or stay at the top. Pure, so the rules can be tested without an engine; `GameStyleTextView` keeps one and lays it out every time something changed.

The position is an offset in lines above the newest line, as in [`LineScroll`](#linescroll): 0 follows the newest line, a larger value stays on the same lines while more arrive. "At the top" is kept as its own intent rather than as a number, so a view opened at line 0 stays at line 0 when the window is resized or the content grows, instead of drifting to whatever offset the old size happened to give.

Every change bumps [`LineScrollState.Version`](#linescrollstate--version), so a view knows when to lay out again.

<a id="linescrollstate--handlesize"></a>

### `float HandleSize { get; }`

The scrollbar handle size for the last layout, as a share of the track.

<a id="linescrollstate--last"></a>

### `LineWindow Last { get; }`

The last plan [`LineScrollState.Layout`](#linescrollstate--layout) made.

<a id="linescrollstate--offset"></a>

### `int Offset { get; }`

Lines above the newest line; 0 follows the newest line.

<a id="linescrollstate--pinnedtotop"></a>

### `bool PinnedToTop { get; }`

True while the reader wants line 0 at the top of the box.

<a id="linescrollstate--scrollbarvalue"></a>

### `float ScrollbarValue { get; }`

The scrollbar handle position for the current position in the last layout's range (0 newest, 1 oldest).

<a id="linescrollstate--total"></a>

### `int Total { get; }`

Lines in the list at the last [`LineScrollState.Layout`](#linescrollstate--layout).

<a id="linescrollstate--version"></a>

### `long Version { get; }`

Grows by one on every change of position or intent.

<a id="linescrollstate--appended"></a>

### `void Appended(int lines)`

`lines` new lines arrived at the end. A view following the newest line keeps following; a view scrolled up moves up with them, so the lines being read stay put.

**Parameters**

- `lines`: How many; zero or less changes nothing.

<a id="linescrollstate--fromscrollbar"></a>

### `void FromScrollbar(float value)`

Moves to where a bottom-to-top scrollbar was dragged (0 newest, 1 oldest), using the last layout's range. Dragging to the very top pins the view there.

**Parameters**

- `value`: Scrollbar value.

<a id="linescrollstate--layout"></a>

### `LineWindow Layout(int total, float boxHeight, float spacing, Func<int, float> heightOf)`

Plans the lines to draw for the current position ([`LineLayout.Plan`](#linelayout--plan)) and keeps the position the plan actually used. Does not bump [`LineScrollState.Version`](#linescrollstate--version).

**Parameters**

- `total`: Lines in the list.
- `boxHeight`: Height of the text box.
- `spacing`: Distance between consecutive lines.
- `heightOf`: Height of line i on its own at the box's width.

<a id="linescrollstate--pagedown"></a>

### `void PageDown()`

Down by a page.

<a id="linescrollstate--pageup"></a>

### `void PageUp()`

Up by a page: the lines wholly visible now, less one line of context.

<a id="linescrollstate--scroll"></a>

### `void Scroll(int lines)`

Scrolls by whole lines, positive towards older lines. Reaching the top pins the view there; any move down unpins it. Clamped to the last layout's range.

**Parameters**

- `lines`: How far.

<a id="linescrollstate--toend"></a>

### `void ToEnd()`

Jumps to the newest line and follows it again.

<a id="linescrollstate--tostart"></a>

### `void ToStart()`

Jumps to line 0 and stays there: how a freshly opened document reads.

<a id="windowrectmath"></a>

## `WindowRectMath`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Console.WindowRectMath` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Placement rules for a draggable, resizable window. Pure, so the rules can be tested without an engine; the game-style window applies them to its RectTransform.

The game keeps a dragged window entirely on screen (`DraggableUI.AdjustPos` clamps the window's half-extents against the screen edges), so these rules do the same: a window never leaves the canvas, and one larger than the canvas is shrunk to fit before it is placed. Candidate for the mod-windows toolkit.

<a id="windowrectmath--defaultheightfraction"></a>

### `const float DefaultHeightFraction = 0.62f`

Share of the canvas height a new window takes.

<a id="windowrectmath--defaultmargin"></a>

### `const float DefaultMargin = 24.0f`

Gap kept between a new window and the canvas edge.

<a id="windowrectmath--defaultwidthfraction"></a>

### `const float DefaultWidthFraction = 0.7f`

Share of the canvas width a new window takes (the IMGUI console used the same).

<a id="windowrectmath--clamp"></a>

### `static WindowRect Clamp(WindowRect rect, float canvasWidth, float canvasHeight, float minWidth, float minHeight)`

Keeps a window on the canvas: first shrinks it to fit (never below the minimum), then moves it so no edge is outside. A window still larger than the canvas at its minimum size is pinned to the top-left corner, so its title bar and close button stay reachable.

**Parameters**

- `rect`: The window.
- `canvasWidth`: Canvas width.
- `canvasHeight`: Canvas height.
- `minWidth`: Smallest width.
- `minHeight`: Smallest height.

<a id="windowrectmath--default"></a>

### `static WindowRect Default(float canvasWidth, float canvasHeight, float minWidth, float minHeight)`

Where a window opens the first time: the default share of the canvas, horizontally centred, a quarter of the free height down from the top.

- `canvasHeight`: Canvas height in canvas units.
- `minWidth`: Smallest width the window's layout works at.
- `minHeight`: Smallest height the window's layout works at.

<a id="windowrectmath--resize"></a>

### `static WindowRect Resize(WindowRect rect, float deltaWidth, float deltaHeight, float canvasWidth, float canvasHeight, float minWidth, float minHeight)`

A window resized from its bottom-right grip: the top-left corner stays put, the size follows the pointer, never below the minimum and never past the canvas edge.

Converts a pointer movement in screen pixels (Y up, as Unity reports it) into canvas units with Y down.
